lesson.title: Other law and the limits of an exception
lesson.summary: Keep other Union prohibitions and independent evidence checks after a biometric exception assessment.

prerequisites.reason: The check applies the principle that other applicable law continues to govern the practice.
An Article 5 conclusion leaves a separate test under other applicable Union prohibitions.
The output-based decision restriction concerns the real-time identification system already defined.

blocks: An Article 5 exception result is not complete legal permission. Paragraph 8 preserves **prohibitions under other Union law**. The non-law-enforcement biometric-processing clause expressly leaves GDPR Article 9 unaffected.

For a non-police biometric use, check applicable privacy rules, including the special-category prohibition and available legal conditions. Being outside the public-space law-enforcement test does not itself provide a data-processing basis.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1), second subparagraph; 5(3), final sentence; 5(8)

blocks: The separate **no adverse legal decision solely on output** rule applies to real-time remote identification. A decision producing an adverse legal effect cannot be based solely on its output.
A match signal is not a substitute for independent evidence and proper procedure. This is a substantive decision limit even after the system's use has satisfied the exception safeguards.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1), second subparagraph; 5(3), final sentence; 5(8)

blocks: Fictional Northbridge search returns a match, and officials propose an adverse legal decision using only that output. The final-sentence limit remains relevant despite an authorised operation.

Changed case: the use is a private non-law-enforcement verification. The specific public-space law-enforcement ban may differ; applicable privacy, biometric, accuracy and other legal obligations remain to be checked.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1), second subparagraph; 5(3), final sentence; 5(8)

blocks: Separate conclusions: the specific Article 5 test; Annex III/Article 6 classification; rules governing processing; and any adverse decision's evidence/procedure. Each result answers a different question.
Record unresolved facts plainly. Do not write 'fully compliant' from a single exception finding, a technical accuracy claim or the absence of a particular prohibition.
